skill.name: devflow-tdd-enforcer
skill.description: Enforces test-first order in DevFlow TASKS.md files by blocking implementation tasks from being completed before matching test tasks.
skill.summary: Blocks DevFlow task updates that complete implementation before tests.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline examples, regex strings, and sample task checklist text in SKILL.md. No executable shell code, external command invocation, reconnaissance behavior, or prompt-injection attempt was found in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: 💡 SKIP: Add `@skip-tdd-check` comment or set SKIP_TDD_ENFORCER=1
- [ ] **T011** [US1] Test user registration with valid data
- [ ] **T010** [US1] Test user registration with valid data (write FAILING test)
- [x] **T010** [US1] Test user registration with valid data
- [ ] **T029** [US3] Test password reset with valid email
**Rationale**: Avoid duplication ("不重不漏" principle). planner agent owns TDD generation logic, guardr

content.value_statement: Teams can drift from test-first discipline when task files are edited by hand. This skill defines checks that block implementation completion until related tests are complete.
actual_capabilities: Defines a PreToolUse trigger for edits to DevFlow requirements TASKS.md files.
Identifies task patterns where implementation is complete before related tests.
Documents regex patterns for test-first ordering violations.
Provides a blocking message for TDD violations during file edits.
Explains session, file marker, and environment variable skip conditions.
limitations: It documents guardrail behavior but does not include executable hook code in this package.
It targets DevFlow TASKS.md files and does not audit general source code.
Regex checks cannot confirm that tests were executed or failed first.
Skip conditions allow users to bypass enforcement when configured.

use_cases.title: Keep Story Work Test First
use_cases.description: Prevent implementation tasks from being marked complete while matching test tasks remain open.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering teams using DevFlow task files

use_cases.title: Review Manual Task Edits
use_cases.description: Catch hand-edited task lists that reverse the intended test-before-implementation sequence.

use_cases.title: Document TDD Exceptions
use_cases.description: Use explicit skip mechanisms for hotfixes or batch work while preserving the normal policy.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Task Order
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a DevFlow task list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my TASKS.md entries and tell me whether any implementation task is complete before its related test task.

prompt_templates.title: Fix TDD Violations
prompt_templates.prompt: Reorder these DevFlow tasks so every test task appears before the implementation task it validates.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Guardrail Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup for a team workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create TDD guardrail guidance for our DevFlow requirements files, including violation patterns and approved skip cases.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Workflow Exceptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these TDD skip requests and identify which ones are justified, risky, or missing follow-up test work.

output_examples.input: A TASKS.md edit marks an implementation task complete while the paired test task remains open.
output_examples.output: The skill reports a TDD ordering violation and directs the user to complete or reorder the test task first.

output_examples.input: A hotfix requires bypassing the normal TDD task order for one file.
output_examples.output: The skill points to documented skip mechanisms and keeps the exception explicit for later review.

output_examples.input: A user story lists tests first and implementation second, with both completed in order.
output_examples.output: The skill treats the task sequence as compliant with the documented test-first policy.

best_practices: Keep test tasks adjacent to the implementation tasks they validate.
Use skip conditions only for documented exceptions with follow-up test work.
Review generated TASKS.md files before marking implementation tasks complete.
anti_patterns: Marking implementation complete while the related test task is still open.
Using global skip settings as a normal development workflow.
Relying on task order checks as proof that tests actually passed.

faq.question: What files does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets DevFlow requirements TASKS.md files described by the skill documentation.

faq.question: Does it run my test suite?
faq.answer: No. It checks task ordering guidance and does not execute tests.

faq.question: Can users bypass the guardrail?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents session, file marker, and environment variable skip conditions.

faq.question: Is this only for TDD teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for teams that require tests before implementation work is completed.

faq.question: Does it generate DevFlow tasks?
faq.answer: No. It describes enforcement after tasks already exist.

faq.question: Can it validate real code coverage?
faq.answer: No. Coverage validation must come from separate test and reporting tools.
